Reform area: Reform Area 3: Enhancing International Trade Facilitation and Attracting Investment
Outcome: The number of active residents in the technological park reached at least 50. (2023 baseline: 0) (Source: AIDT).
Description: 1.10 To enhance investment opportunities, mobilize financing for infrastructure development and climate-related initiatives, the government (i) updated the regulatory framework for the issuance of local currency bond at market rates and raised TJS100 million, through issuance of local bonds; and (ii) updated the regulatory framework for issuance of Green Bonds during FY2024.

Reform area: Reform Area 3: Enhancing International Trade Facilitation and Attracting Investment
Outcome: The number of active residents in the technological park reached at least 50. (2023 baseline: 0) (Source: AIDT).
Description: 1.8 To promote innovation and adaptation of modern technology and enhance opportunities for climate-friendly private sector investment, the amendments and additions to the Law on Technological Parks were approved by the government. The amended law provides clarity regarding: (i) creation and operations of technological parks; (ii) shapes of the technological parks; and (iii) rights of non-resident foreign tenants within such parks.

Reform area: Reform Area 3: Enhancing International Trade Facilitation and Attracting Investment
Outcome: The number of active residents in the technological park reached at least 50. (2023 baseline: 0) (Source: AIDT).
Description: 1.9 To facilitate export diversification and promote climate-friendly private sector, the MOF and the Agency for Export, through an order, jointly approved: (i) a framework to support exporters through: (a) financial incentives for climate-friendly exporters or for traditional export industries to transition to climate-friendly operations; (b) trade facilitation services through export documentation and compliance assistance; and (c) creation of export acceleration program for new and existing exports to enter into foreign markets;
(ii) at least 15% of the funding was allocated for women-led climate-friendly entrepreneurs involved in exports. (iii) the government allocated TJS20 million to the Export Agency of Tajikistan to support exporters.

Reform area: Reform Area 3: Enhancing International Trade Facilitation and Attracting Investment
Outcome: The number of active residents in the technological park reached at least 50. (2023 baseline: 0) (Source: AIDT).
Description: 2.10 (i) To promote digital innovation and sustainable entrepreneurship, the Government: (a) established the Technological Park for Software Products and Information Technologies; and (b) delegated management rights to the Agency for Innovation and Digital Technologies.
(ii) To strengthen industrial resilience to climate risks, accelerate low-carbon transformation, and align national industrial policy with the GEDS, the MINT established the Division for the Development of Green Industry within its organizational structure as a dedicated unit.

Reform area: Reform Area 3: Enhancing International Trade Facilitation and Attracting Investment
Outcome: The number of active residents in the technological park reached at least 50. (2023 baseline: 0) (Source: AIDT).
Description: 2.11 To boost export competitiveness, reduce institutional fragmentation and strengthen integration into global green value chains, the Government of Tajikistan issued a decree, covering: (i) Designating the Export Agency as the central executive body of the Republic of Tajikistan responsible for implementing state policy in the area of export. (ii) Mandating the Export Agency for development and maintenance of exporters database and assisting export entities to start e-commerce.

Reform area: Reform Area 3: Enhancing International Trade Facilitation and Attracting Investment
Outcome: The number of active residents in the technological park reached at least 50. (2023 baseline: 0) (Source: AIDT).
Description: 2.12 (i) To facilitate small exporters of sustainable products, the Export Agency of Tajikistan: (a) Established the Small Exporter Facilitation Unit as a dedicated support unit within its organizational structure; (b) Allocated three staff positions for the unit, with at least one reserved for women to promote gender diversity. (c) Mandated the unit for conducting a diagnostic for implementation of credit insurance guarantee system for small exporters in Tajikistan.
(ii) To expand export opportunities for the women led enterprises climate-friendly businesses, the Export Agency issued an order to the State Unitary Enterprise “Tajagropromexport” to prioritize procurement from climate friendly businesses led by women, with at least 15% of total purchases sourced from such enterprises.

Reform area: Reform Area 3: Enhancing International Trade Facilitation and Attracting Investment
Outcome: The number of active residents in the technological park reached at least 50. (2023 baseline: 0) (Source: AIDT).
Description: 2.13 (i) To integrate climate objectives into fiscal policy and planning, the MOF established a dedicated “Division of Analysis of Internal Debt, Government Securities Issuance and Green/Climate Financing”, with the mandate of: (a) Developing and implementing climate-informed budget strategies and expenditure frameworks (b) Coordinating with line ministries, development partners, and climate finance institutions; (c) Mobilizing private climate finance by leveraging public investments and budgetary instruments; and (d) ensuring gender inclusion by appointing a female director to lead the new division
(ii) in accordance with its mandate, the newly established division issued sovereign green bonds valued at TJS200 million in 2025 to mobilize financing for climate-related investments.

Reform area: Reform Area 2: Improving Governance, Advancing Transparency and Driving Digital Transformation
Outcome: The number of active e-commerce businesses increased to 6. (2022 baseline: 4) (Source: MEDT, TAJSTAT).
Description: 1.4 To improve fiscal transparency and accountability, the MOF issued an order to (i) establish a dedicated unit responsible for collecting, organizing, and publishing GFS data in accordance with the GFSM 2014 framework; and (ii) mandated the quarterly publication of GFS data.

Reform area: Reform Area 2: Improving Governance, Advancing Transparency and Driving Digital Transformation
Outcome: The number of active e-commerce businesses increased to 6. (2022 baseline: 4) (Source: MEDT, TAJSTAT).
Description: 1.5 To improve infrastructure governance, ensure better infrastructure for private business and address climate change challenges, the Government of Tajikistan completed the PIMA and climate PIMA to identify inefficiencies towards public investment management practices in Tajikistan.

Reform area: Reform Area 2: Improving Governance, Advancing Transparency and Driving Digital Transformation
Outcome: The number of active e-commerce businesses increased to 6. (2022 baseline: 4) (Source: MEDT, TAJSTAT).
Description: 1.6 To strengthen compliance management through the progressive implementation of risk-based approaches, the Tax Committee approved the compliance improvement plan for large taxpayers in the construction sector.

Reform area: Reform Area 2: Improving Governance, Advancing Transparency and Driving Digital Transformation
Outcome: The number of active e-commerce businesses increased to 6. (2022 baseline: 4) (Source: MEDT, TAJSTAT).
Description: 2.5 To strengthen fiscal risk management related to SOEs, PPPs and climate, the MOF adopted a ministerial decree on the operationalization of the Fiscal Risk Registers, and the decree mandated: (i) principal definitions, purpose and key steps of maintaining the fiscal risk register for SOEs, PPPs and Climate-related fiscal risks; and (ii) methodology for recognizing and measuring fiscal risks.

Reform area: Reform Area 2: Improving Governance, Advancing Transparency and Driving Digital Transformation
Outcome: The number of active e-commerce businesses increased to 6. (2022 baseline: 4) (Source: MEDT, TAJSTAT).
Description: 2.6 To strengthen fiscal transparency and align budget planning with climate and environmental priorities, the MOF issued a ministerial order directing the State Budget Directorate to integrate Climate Budget Tagging (CBT) into the state budget process. The Order: (i) mandated the development of methodological guidelines for climate budget tagging and to be approved before February 2026; and (ii) required the integration of climate and environmental aspects into the Government Resolution on preparation of the 2027-2029 state budget.

Reform area: Reform Area 2: Improving Governance, Advancing Transparency and Driving Digital Transformation
Outcome: The number of active e-commerce businesses increased to 6. (2022 baseline: 4) (Source: MEDT, TAJSTAT).
Description: 2.7 (i) To accelerate Tajikistan's digital transformation and promote innovation-driven growth, the Tax Committee approved a simplified tax regime for innovative and technological activities in the Technological Park, established in Dushanbe, including its: (a) exemption from social tax; and (b) exemption from the VAT & CIT.
(ii) To promote environmental sustainability and align fiscal policy with ecological priorities, the Government increased excise duties on: (a) motor gasoline from €55 to €70 per metric ton; and (b) petroleum gas oil from €8 to €15 per metric ton.

Reform area: Reform Area 2: Improving Governance, Advancing Transparency and Driving Digital Transformation
Outcome: The number of active e-commerce businesses increased to 6. (2022 baseline: 4) (Source: MEDT, TAJSTAT).
Description: 2.8 (i) To reduce institutional fragmentation, accelerate digital transformation, improve citizen access to services, and strengthen government-wide accountability, the Government: (a) designated the AIDT as the state authorized body in the sphere of innovation activity; (b) transferred responsibility on the rules for maintaining the Register of Public Services from the Ministry of Justice to AIDT; (c) mandated AIDT the responsibility of leading the finalization of the Rules for Optimization and Automation of Public Service Delivery.
(ii) To enhance the acceptability and enforceability of digital payments, the Government amended the Law on State Services to formally recognize electronic documents confirming non-cash payments—including electronic receipts, paid orders, and transaction notifications from payment service providers—as legally valid once received in the service provider's non-cash payment accounting system.

Reform area: Reform Area 2: Improving Governance, Advancing Transparency and Driving Digital Transformation
Outcome: The number of active e-commerce businesses increased to 6. (2022 baseline: 4) (Source: MEDT, TAJSTAT).
Description: 2.8 To enhance national cybersecurity and promote good governance, the Government of Tajikistan through a Presidential Decree: (i) established the State Institution “Data Protection Center”; (ii) approved the Charter and the Structure of the Center; and (iii) set the maximum number of the staff positions, of the Center.

Reform area: Reform Area 1: Strengthening Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and Fostering Green Employment
Outcome: Number of Presidential grants for women entrepreneurs increased from 80 recipients to 120 (2022 baseline: 80) (Source: MOF data).
Description: 1.1 To foster climate-friendly investment and increase green jobs in the private sector, the MOF approved regulations through a decree to establish: (i) criteria for identifying climate-friendly SMEs; and (ii) a policy for state-owned banks to provide subsidized financing to climate-friendly SMEs.

Reform area: Reform Area 1: Strengthening Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and Fostering Green Employment
Outcome: Number of Presidential grants for women entrepreneurs increased from 80 recipients to 120 (2022 baseline: 80) (Source: MOF data).
Description: 1.2 The MEDT operationalized a unit within the MEDT for implementing the recently approved Green Economy Development Strategy (GEDS) and (i) allocated three positions for the unit, with at least one position allocated for women within the unit to promote gender diversity; and (ii) approved the workplan for the unit.

Reform area: Reform Area 1: Strengthening Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and Fostering Green Employment
Outcome: Number of Presidential grants for women entrepreneurs increased from 80 recipients to 120 (2022 baseline: 80) (Source: MOF data).
Description: 1.3 To enhance financing opportunities for the SME sector: (i) The MOF issued an order approving a policy to strengthen the leasing sector by addressing key bottlenecks such as required regulatory and taxation issues and provided criteria on climate-friendly businesses. (ii) The government increased state budget allocation for presidential grants for women-led enterprises from TJS2.5 million to TJS5.0 million, with up to 10% of this grant allocated to climate-friendly businesses.

Reform area: Reform Area 1: Strengthening Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and Fostering Green Employment
Outcome: Number of Presidential grants for women entrepreneurs increased from 80 recipients to 120 (2022 baseline: 80) (Source: MOF data).
Description: 2.1 To strengthen the climate-friendly SMEs ecosystem, catalyze green entrepreneurship, and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy: (i) the MOF allocated $2.0 million for state-owned banks to support climate-friendly SMEs with subsidize loans; and (ii) at least 20% of the $2.0 million lending portfolio is earmarked for SMEs led by women (per criteria set in endnote b).

Action 1: 1.8 To promote innovation and adaptation of modern technology and enhance opportunities for climate-friendly private sector investment, the amendments and additions to the Law on Technological Parks were approved by the government. The amended law provides clarity regarding: (i) creation and operations of technological parks; (ii) shapes of the technological parks; and (iii) rights of non-resident foreign tenants within such parks.
Action 2: 1.9 To facilitate export diversification and promote climate-friendly private sector, the MOF and the Agency for Export, through an order, jointly approved: (i) a framework to support exporters through: (a) financial incentives for climate-friendly exporters or for traditional export industries to transition to climate-friendly operations; (b) trade facilitation services through export documentation and compliance assistance; and (c) creation of export acceleration program for new and existing exports to enter into foreign markets;
(ii) at least 15% of the funding was allocated for women-led climate-friendly entrepreneurs involved in exports. (iii) the government allocated TJS20 million to the Export Agency of Tajikistan to support exporters.
Action 3: 1.10 To enhance investment opportunities, mobilize financing for infrastructure development and climate-related initiatives, the government (i) updated the regulatory framework for the issuance of local currency bond at market rates and raised TJS100 million, through issuance of local bonds; and (ii) updated the regulatory framework for issuance of Green Bonds during FY2024.
Action 1: 2.10 (i) To promote digital innovation and sustainable entrepreneurship, the Government: (a) established the Technological Park for Software Products and Information Technologies; and (b) delegated management rights to the Agency for Innovation and Digital Technologies.
(ii) To strengthen industrial resilience to climate risks, accelerate low-carbon transformation, and align national industrial policy with the GEDS, the MINT established the Division for the Development of Green Industry within its organizational structure as a dedicated unit.
Action 2: 2.11 To boost export competitiveness, reduce institutional fragmentation and strengthen integration into global green value chains, the Government of Tajikistan issued a decree, covering: (i) Designating the Export Agency as the central executive body of the Republic of Tajikistan responsible for implementing state policy in the area of export. (ii) Mandating the Export Agency for development and maintenance of exporters database and assisting export entities to start e-commerce.
Action 3: 2.12 (i) To facilitate small exporters of sustainable products, the Export Agency of Tajikistan: (a) Established the Small Exporter Facilitation Unit as a dedicated support unit within its organizational structure; (b) Allocated three staff positions for the unit, with at least one reserved for women to promote gender diversity. (c) Mandated the unit for conducting a diagnostic for implementation of credit insurance guarantee system for small exporters in Tajikistan.
(ii) To expand export opportunities for the women led enterprises climate-friendly businesses, the Export Agency issued an order to the State Unitary Enterprise “Tajagropromexport” to prioritize procurement from climate friendly businesses led by women, with at least 15% of total purchases sourced from such enterprises.
Action 4: 2.13 (i) To integrate climate objectives into fiscal policy and planning, the MOF established a dedicated “Division of Analysis of Internal Debt, Government Securities Issuance and Green/Climate Financing”, with the mandate of: (a) Developing and implementing climate-informed budget strategies and expenditure frameworks (b) Coordinating with line ministries, development partners, and climate finance institutions; (c) Mobilizing private climate finance by leveraging public investments and budgetary instruments; and (d) ensuring gender inclusion by appointing a female director to lead the new division
(ii) in accordance with its mandate, the newly established division issued sovereign green bonds valued at TJS200 million in 2025 to mobilize financing for climate-related investments.
